# authwise_guard_tenant_settings (Resource)

Guard's settings for a kit tenant: its labels, the realms its people come from, and whether its devices are swept. Guard has no tenant of its own: its networks and settings are keyed by the kit tenant (`t-…`), and what kit owns about the tenant (its name, slug, status, and the issuer, audience and console client its people sign in through) is read-only here.

guard-control writes the settings once kit reports Guard on the tenant; until then it refuses with `GUARD_NOT_ENABLED`, and a suspended tenant with `TENANT_SUSPENDED`. Each refusal is guard-control's own message.

An attribute left unset is neither written nor reset: it reads back what guard-control holds. Removing one from the configuration later leaves its last value in place; set it explicitly (`realms = []`, `enabled = false`) to change it.

**Destroy writes nothing.** It removes the resource from state and leaves Guard's settings on the tenant. Deleting a tenant from Guard is an operator's task, refused while it has networks or users.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Guard's settings for a kit tenant. Unset attributes are left as
# guard-control holds them; destroying this writes nothing.
resource "authwise_guard_tenant_settings" "acme" {
  tenant_id = "t-01"

  labels = {
    owner = "it"
  }

  config = {
    # Whose people are the tenant's; empty means every realm its issuer routes to.
    users = { realms = ["r-01"] }
    # Revoke the devices of people who no longer hold Guard.
    deprovisioning = { enabled = true }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `tenant_id` (String) The kit tenant's id (`t-…`) the Guard row belongs to. Guard has no tenant of its own since the tenant collapse (tf#65). The provider's `tenant_id` is not used. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `config` (Attributes) Guard's settings for the tenant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `labels` (Map of String) Guard's labels on the tenant. Written whole when it changes.

### Read-Only

- `audience` (String) The Guard audience the tenant's people's tokens carry (`aud`).
- `console_client_id` (String) The Guard console's public client on the tenant's issuer.
- `display_name` (String) The kit tenant's display name.
- `issuer` (String) The issuer the tenant's people sign in at, exactly as their tokens' `iss`.
- `name` (String) The tenant's resource name at guard-control, `tenants/t-…`.
- `plan` (Attributes) The tenant's plan and its caps, read from kit's tenant (guard-control#88). guard-control enforces `devices_limit` and `relay_bytes_limit` (a network over its relay cap reads `pool_capped`) and treats an expired trial as read-only; kit enforces `members_limit` at its invitation. 0 is no cap. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--plan))
- `slug` (String) The kit tenant's slug, which names it in mesh DNS (`<node>.<network>.<slug>.guard.<estate>`). It is kit's, set on the tenant in kit (`awtenant tenants update --slug`, kit 1.83.0 or later); guard-control refuses to write it (`SLUG_MANAGED_BY_IDENTITY`).
- `status` (String) The kit tenant's state (`ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`). Suspension is kit's.

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `deprovisioning` (Attributes) The deprovisioning sweep. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--deprovisioning))
- `users` (Attributes) Where the tenant's people come from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--users))

<a id="nestedatt--config--deprovisioning"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.deprovisioning`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Sweep the tenant's devices: a device a person enrolled keeps working after they lose Guard, because its token refreshes on the node's own identity. The sweep re-checks with guard-control's install credential and revokes each node whose owner no binding reaches any more. It never revokes on a failed read.


<a id="nestedatt--config--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.users`

Optional:

- `realms` (List of String) The realm ids (`r-…`) whose people are the tenant's. Empty means every realm the tenant's issuer routes to.



<a id="nestedatt--plan"></a>
### Nested Schema for `plan`

Read-Only:

- `devices_limit` (Number) The most devices the tenant may enrol; 0 is no cap.
- `members_limit` (Number) The most people the tenant may have; 0 is no cap.
- `plan` (String) `TRIAL`, `FREE`, `TEAM`, `BUSINESS` or `ENTERPRISE`; empty when kit reports none.
- `relay_bytes_limit` (Number) The relay traffic the tenant may use, in bytes; 0 is no cap.
- `trial_ends_at` (String) When a trial ends, RFC 3339; empty otherwise.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the kit tenant's id, or its name at guard-control (tenants/t-01).
terraform import authwise_guard_tenant_settings.acme t-01
```
